body:
I did some investigation, and I've found that this bug happens after you add the duplicated node to the scene tree with `add_child`.

What I think is happening is that when you duplicate the TileMapLayer, the instantiated scene tiles get copied over, but the `tile_map_layer_data` HashMap that should keep track of those scene tiles does not.
So when you add the new node to the tree, the program thinks that there are no instantiated scene tiles, and spawns them in.

A workaround I've found for this is that you remove the TileMapLayer that you want to duplicate from the scene with `remove_child`, wait a process frame so that the scene nodes get removed, duplicate it, then add both TileMapLayers back with `add_child`.
The `remove_child` triggers a `queue_free` for every scene node in the source code resulting in no duplicates.
So the code would look something like this:
```
remove_child(original);
await get_tree().process_frame

var copy: TileMapLayer = original.duplicate();

add_child(original);
add_child(copy);
```

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/d79ff848fa599df0665977623581fe55f558eaee/scene/2d/tile_map_layer.cpp#L1264
Adding `remove_child(node)` above this line in the source code, would eliminate the need for the `await get_tree().process_frame`, but wouldn't fix the issue.

I'm very new to Godot's source code, and C++, so I was just messing around with this, and thought I would share my findings, so someone with more knowledge could maybe fix the problem easier.
Wow yup, full repros on arch/niri, godot 4.4.1 and 4.5beta3. Thanks for the MRP!
